consensus_summary: Consensus treats feet primarily as a person’s walk, path, moral conduct, or course of life (strongly context-dependent), with common alternative strands for gospel messengers’ beautiful/shod feet, dominion (enemies under feet), humility/servanthood/cleansing via footwashing, and sitting at feet in discipleship/worship.
book_summary: Feet symbolize a person’s walk or conduct—the way that must remain clean (tied to John 13:10).
consensus_core_identification: Feet as the symbol of a person’s walk/conduct/moral path or direction of life.
book_core_identification: Feet as a person’s walk or conduct, specifically the way that must remain clean.
boundary_disagreement: Book makes ongoing cleanliness a definitional condition of the walk/conduct symbol and centers the John 13 washing motif, whereas consensus keeps walk/conduct as the broad primary and treats cleansing/humility as a related but distinct common alternative.
rationale: Both identify the same central referent (walk/conduct). The book does not replace it with dominion, messengers, euphemism, or another strand; it only tightens the boundary by requiring that the way remain clean and by anchoring the entry solely to the foot-washing text. This is a precision/narrowing refinement of extension and conditions, not a contradictory core.
strongest_objection: John 13:10 directly supports residual cleansing of already-washed persons rather than the general ‘walk/conduct’ metaphor; the book’s primary gloss therefore leans on an unstated conventional link while the printed citation alone is thinner for the walk claim than the consensus’s multi-verse basis.
